subtopic: Deciding what to do with pocket money
subtype: Approach: waiting a few days before buying [Thinking]
passage: The toy robot in the shop window had a sign: SALE ENDS SUNDAY. Vishal wanted it so badly his palms tingled. "Can we buy it now?" His mother shook her head. "Wait three days. If you still want it, we will go." It was Thursday; Sunday felt far away. On Friday he thought of the robot twice, on Saturday once, mostly while passing the shop. On Sunday morning Amandeep came round with a pack of cricket cards. Vishal ran his eyes over the shiny cards and saw that his pocket money would stretch to four packs. "Not the robot," he told his mother. She smiled.

qa.q: How long did Vishal agree to wait?
qa.a: He agreed to wait three days.

qa.q: What was Vishal feeling when he first saw the robot?
qa.a: Eager and longing, since his palms tingled and he wanted to buy it immediately.

qa.q: What other approach could Vishal use to test whether he really wants something, and why?
qa.a: He could write down what else the money could buy and compare, because seeing the choices shows what matters more.

qa.q: How might Vishal's mother feel about the waiting rule?
qa.a: She is hopeful that waiting will help him think, and she smiles when he chooses for himself.

grounding: A boy agrees to wait three days before buying a toy, and by then he prefers to spend on cricket cards.

subtopic: Deciding what to do with pocket money
subtype: Approach: waiting a few days before buying [Thinking]
passage: On Thursday evening, in the toy corner of the Rajouri market, Uday could not stop looking at a remote-control jeep with flashing wheels. It would take almost all his birthday money. "Mumma, please, today?" His mother, Bhavna, said, "Let's both wait three days. If you still want it on Sunday, we'll come back." Uday nodded, but he sulked in the auto all the way home. On Friday he drew the jeep in his notebook. On Saturday he mentioned it once. On Sunday morning a friend showed him a new pack of cricket cards, and Uday spent an hour sorting his own. When Bhavna asked about the jeep, he thought for a while. "It's nice... but the wheels will only flash for a week. The cards I'll keep trading all year. I'll keep the money for those."

qa.q: What did Uday want to buy at the market?
qa.a: A remote-control jeep with flashing wheels.

qa.q: How had Uday's feelings changed by Sunday?
qa.a: His excitement had faded; he felt calm and thoughtful enough to decide the cards would give him longer-lasting fun.

qa.q: Which other approach might suit Uday next time, and why?
qa.a: He could put the jeep and the cards side by side and ask which he would still enjoy in a month, since that shows lasting value before he spends.

qa.q: How might Bhavna see the waiting plan?
qa.a: She is probably relieved that Uday chose for himself instead of being refused, so there was no fight at the shop.

grounding: A boy agrees to wait three days before buying a toy and finds his wish has faded in favour of cricket cards.

passage:
"Mummy, it's day three," Kunal announced at breakfast.
Jyoti looked up from her tea. "Day three of what?"
"The battle top. You said wait three days, then decide."
"I did. So? Still want it?"
Kunal chewed his paratha slowly. "On day one I wanted it so much my stomach hurt. Yesterday I only thought about it at night. Today..." He shrugged. "Rohit's top broke in one week. And the new cricket cards have come to the shop."
"So which is it?"
"The top is fun for five minutes. The cards I can swap with the whole building. I think I'll keep the money for cards."
"You're sure? I won't say I told you so."
Kunal grinned. "You just did, Mummy."

qa.q: What did Kunal want before the three days of waiting?
How did Kunal's feelings about the top change over the three days?
qa.a: On day one he wanted it so badly his stomach hurt; by day three the excitement had faded and he felt calm enough to choose the cards.

qa.q: What else could Kunal have done to test his wish?
qa.a: He could have tried a friend's top for an afternoon, since playing with something often shows whether the wanting will last.

qa.q: What is it like for Jyoti to hear Kunal's decision?
qa.a: Jyoti seems amused and pleased, teasing that she won't say she told him so. 😊

grounding: A boy waits three days before buying a toy and decides to keep the money for cricket cards instead.
